To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

allophycocayanin B from Rh. violacea is a new allophycocoyanin‐like phycobiliprotein, which is characterized by a long wavelength absorbing shoulder and fluorescence emission, respectively, and which can be isolated in a ‘native’ state.
allophycocanin B from Rhoddella violacea is a model for the core of rhodophycean phycobilisosomes.
the phycobiliproteins allophycocayanin A and B, isolated from the red alga Rhodella violace, are trimeric in nature and the linker polypeptide Lc 13,5APB is localized in allophycycyanin B.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation of allophycobyanin B from the hemidiscal phycobilisomal complex of the red alga Rhodella violace.
the isolation of allophycocyamin B from Rhodalla violacea, its spectroscopic characterization and the construction of a structural model of the hemidiscoid phycobilisomal core of Rhodalla violaceae.
the structure, the localization and the stoichiometry of allophycocyamin B and its linker polypeptides in the phycobilliosome core of Rhodella violacea.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
allophycocayanin B is a ‘trimeric‘ allophycocanin complex, consisting of two α‐, one β‐ and one α∗‐apoprotein and two Lc 13,5APB linker polypeptides.
allophycocayanin B is a ‘trimeric’, allophycocaynin complex which contains one α‐ and two β‐subunits and one linker polypeptide Lc 13,5APB.
the allophycocianins in the phycobionts of the rhodophyte algae are not identical with respect to their composition of the α and β subunits and the linker polypeptides.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
APB is a model for the core from hemidisocoidal phycobiliosomes of the Rhodophyceae.
the allophycocayanin B of Rhodella is a ‘trimeric complex’, consisting of three α and three β‐subunits.
allophycocayanin B represents the first isolated ‘trimeric‘ complex of rhodophycean phycobilisosomes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
allophycocayanin B is a new component of phycobilisomal cores of red algae.
the allophycocayanin B complex, which is a part of phycobilisomal core, is a trimeric complex, which contains two allophycocayin α‐subunits and two allophycocyain β‐subunits.
the linker polypeptide Lc 13APB has a special role in the construction of the phycobillisome core.
